#### LCN-001: ACK cluster's API server has a public endpoint

**Severity:** Medium · **Reads:** Container Service (ACK) clusters · [Alibaba Cloud docs](https://www.alibabacloud.com/help/en/ack/ack-managed-and-ack-dedicated/user-guide/control-public-access-to-the-api-server-of-a-cluster)

The Kubernetes API server answers on the internet. Its authentication is all that stands between anyone and the cluster, and a leaked kubeconfig or a vulnerability in the API server is exploitable from anywhere.

**How to fix**

In the ACK console → the cluster → Basic Information, unbind the EIP from the API server and reach it through the VPC (a bastion, VPN or Cloud Shell). If it must stay public, restrict its SLB with an access control list.

#### LCN-003: Function's HTTP trigger needs no authentication

**Severity:** Medium · **Reads:** Function Compute functions and triggers (environment variables scanned for credentials, never stored) · [Alibaba Cloud docs](https://www.alibabacloud.com/help/en/functioncompute/fc-3-0/user-guide/http-triggers-overview)

Anyone who finds the trigger's URL can call the function as often as they like, and every bug in it is reachable from the internet.

**How to fix**

If the function isn't meant to be public, set the HTTP trigger's authentication to Signature or JWT. If it is, make sure it checks its callers itself and limit what its RAM role can do.

### Alibaba Cloud: Identity & access

#### LID-001: Main account has an AccessKey

**Severity:** Critical · **Reads:** Account identity and alias · [Alibaba Cloud docs](https://www.alibabacloud.com/help/en/ram/use-cases/ensure-security-of-alibaba-cloud-resources)

The main account (root) can do everything in Alibaba Cloud, and no policy limits its AccessKey. Anyone who obtains it, from a laptop, a script or a CI variable, owns the account. Alibaba Cloud recommends that the main account have no AccessKey at all.

**How to fix**

1. Move whatever uses the main account's AccessKey to a RAM user with only the permissions it needs (for Keelson, the read-only policy from the Add accounts flow).
2. Sign in as the main account, open AccessKey management, and disable, then delete, its AccessKeys.

#### LID-013: Main account has no MFA

**Severity:** Critical · **Reads:** Main account's AccessKeys and MFA (RAM's security practice report) · [Alibaba Cloud docs](https://www.alibabacloud.com/help/en/account/user-guide/enable-the-account-protection-feature)

The main account can do everything, including closing the account and every RAM user's access. With a password alone, one phished or reused password hands all of it over.

**How to fix**

Sign in as the main account, open Security Settings, and bind a virtual MFA device or a passkey. Keep the recovery details somewhere only the account's owners can reach.

#### LID-002: RAM user can sign in to the console without MFA

**Severity:** High · **Reads:** RAM users, their AccessKeys, MFA and console access · [Alibaba Cloud docs](https://www.alibabacloud.com/help/en/ram/user-guide/bind-an-mfa-device-to-a-ram-user)

The user's console password is the only thing protecting their access. A reused or phished password is enough to sign in. When the account requires MFA at sign-in, a user without a device is asked to bind one at their next sign-in, so whoever signs in first with the password, the user or an attacker, binds it.

**How to fix**

Bind an MFA device to the user in RAM → Users → the user → Authentication, or have them bind one now. Then require MFA at sign-in for every user under RAM → Settings → Security Settings.

#### LID-014: RAM users can create their own AccessKeys

**Severity:** Medium · **Reads:** RAM security settings: MFA at sign-in, and whether users manage their own AccessKeys · [Alibaba Cloud docs](https://www.alibabacloud.com/help/en/ram/user-guide/manage-security-settings-of-ram-users)

Any RAM user, or anyone holding their console session, can create an AccessKey for themselves. The key works without MFA and outside any sign-in network limits, lasts until someone deletes it, and nobody reviewed it being made.

**How to fix**

In RAM → Settings → Security Settings → RAM user security settings, turn off Manage AccessKeys. Administrators then create keys for the program users that need them.

#### LID-015: RAM user is used both by a person and by programs

**Severity:** Low · **Reads:** RAM users, their AccessKeys, MFA and console access · [Alibaba Cloud docs](https://www.alibabacloud.com/help/en/ram/user-guide/create-a-ram-user)

The user signs in to the console and also has an active AccessKey. Alibaba Cloud recommends separate users for people and programs: the key skips the person's MFA, it is copied into scripts tied to someone who will leave, and the person's access can't be reviewed apart from what the programs need.

**How to fix**

Create a RAM user with OpenAPI access only for the program, give it only the permissions the program needs, move the program to its AccessKey, and delete the person's AccessKey.

#### LID-003: AccessKey is older than 90 days

**Severity:** Medium · **Reads:** RAM users, their AccessKeys, MFA and console access · [Alibaba Cloud docs](https://www.alibabacloud.com/help/en/ram/user-guide/create-an-accesskey-pair)

Long-lived AccessKeys end up in scripts, CI variables and laptops. The longer one lives, the more places it has been copied to, and the longer a leaked copy stays useful.

**How to fix**

Create a new AccessKey for the user, move whatever uses the old one over to it, then disable and delete the old one. Where possible, use a RAM role instead (an ECS instance RAM role, or OIDC from CI).

#### LID-004: AccessKey unused for 90 days

**Severity:** Medium · **Reads:** RAM users, their AccessKeys, MFA and console access · [Alibaba Cloud docs](https://www.alibabacloud.com/help/en/ram/user-guide/view-the-accesskey-pairs-of-a-ram-user)

An AccessKey nobody uses is still a working credential. If it leaked, nobody would notice it being used.

**How to fix**

Disable the AccessKey in RAM → Users → the user → AccessKey, wait to see if anything breaks, then delete it.

#### LID-005: Console password unused for 90 days

**Severity:** Low · **Reads:** RAM users, their AccessKeys, MFA and console access · [Alibaba Cloud docs](https://www.alibabacloud.com/help/en/ram/user-guide/manage-console-logon-settings-for-a-ram-user)

A console sign-in that nobody uses is a password that can still be guessed or phished, with no owner watching for it.

**How to fix**

Turn off console access for the user in RAM → Users → the user → Authentication, or delete the user if nobody needs it.

#### LID-006: Password policy is weak

**Severity:** Medium · **Reads:** RAM password policy, RAM users, their AccessKeys, MFA and console access · [Alibaba Cloud docs](https://www.alibabacloud.com/help/en/ram/user-guide/configure-a-password-policy-for-ram-users)

RAM users who sign in to the console choose their own passwords. Without a minimum length, reuse prevention or a lockout after failed attempts, short or recycled passwords are accepted and can be guessed.

**How to fix**

In RAM → Settings → Security Settings → Password Strength, require at least 14 characters, prevent reuse of recent passwords and lock users out after a few failed attempts in an hour.

#### LID-007: Administrator has a long-lived AccessKey

**Severity:** High · **Reads:** RAM users, their AccessKeys, MFA and console access, RAM policies and who they're attached to (documents reduced to what they allow, never stored) · [Alibaba Cloud docs](https://www.alibabacloud.com/help/en/ram/product-overview/best-practices-for-identity-and-access-control)

This RAM user can do anything in the account, and has an AccessKey that works until someone deletes it. A key leaked from a laptop or a CI variable gives an attacker the whole account.

**How to fix**

Use a RAM role for administrative work (assumed with the user's console sign-in and MFA, or from CI through OIDC), then delete the user's AccessKeys. If a tool needs a key, give it its own user with only the permissions it needs.

#### LID-008: RAM role can be assumed by any Alibaba Cloud account

**Severity:** Critical · **Reads:** RAM roles and their trust policies · [Alibaba Cloud docs](https://www.alibabacloud.com/help/en/ram/user-guide/edit-the-trust-policy-of-a-ram-role)

The role's trust policy lets the principal "*" assume it without a condition. Anyone with an Alibaba Cloud account can get the role's permissions in yours.

**How to fix**

Open the role in RAM → Roles → Trust Policy and replace "*" with the accounts or services that should assume it. Add a condition on sts:ExternalId for a vendor's account.

#### LID-009: Custom policy allows every action on every resource

**Severity:** Medium · **Reads:** RAM policies and who they're attached to (documents reduced to what they allow, never stored) · [Alibaba Cloud docs](https://www.alibabacloud.com/help/en/ram/user-guide/policy-structure-and-syntax)

The policy is a second AdministratorAccess under another name. Whoever it is attached to is an administrator, which reviews that look for AdministratorAccess will miss.

**How to fix**

Open the policy in RAM → Permissions → Policies and narrow its actions and resources to what its users need, or detach it and use AdministratorAccess where full access is intended.

#### LID-010: RAM role trusts an Alibaba Cloud account outside the entity without a condition

**Severity:** Medium · **Reads:** RAM roles and their trust policies · [Alibaba Cloud docs](https://www.alibabacloud.com/help/en/ram/user-guide/edit-the-trust-policy-of-a-ram-role)

Another company's Alibaba Cloud account can assume this role with nothing but its own permissions. If that account is a vendor's, any of the vendor's other customers may be able to make it act on your account; if it is an old partner or a forgotten account, it still has the access.

**How to fix**

1. Open the role in RAM → Roles → Trust Policy.
2. If the other account is one of yours, add it to this entity in Keelson.
3. If it is a vendor's, add a condition that requires the external ID they gave you (sts:ExternalId).
4. If nobody uses the role any more, delete it.

#### LID-011: RAM identity can give itself more access

**Severity:** High · **Reads:** RAM policies and who they're attached to (documents reduced to what they allow, never stored) · [Alibaba Cloud docs](https://www.alibabacloud.com/help/en/ram/user-guide/policy-elements)

Its policies let it attach policies, change a policy's version, create AccessKeys or console passwords for others, or hand a role to a new instance or function. Any of these turns its limited access into whatever it chooses, up to administrator.

**How to fix**

Remove the listed actions from the identity's policies, or limit their Resource to what it really manages. Keep RAM administration with a small group of administrators who sign in with MFA.

#### LID-012: GitHub Actions in any repository can assume this RAM role

**Severity:** Critical · **Attack path** · **Reads:** RAM roles and their trust policies · [Alibaba Cloud docs](https://www.alibabacloud.com/help/en/ram/user-guide/manage-an-oidc-idp)

The role trusts GitHub's OIDC provider without limiting the token's subject to your repositories. A workflow in anyone's repository, on any GitHub account, can get a token GitHub signs and assume the role.

**How to fix**

Open the role in RAM → Roles → Trust Policy and add a condition on oidc:sub naming your organization and repository, for example repo:your-org/your-repo:ref:refs/heads/main or repo:your-org/your-repo:environment:production.

#### XP-022: RAM role trusts GitHub repositories outside the entity

**Severity:** High · **Spans providers** · **Reads:** RAM roles and their trust policies · [GitHub docs](https://docs.github.com/en/actions/security-for-github-actions/security-hardening-your-deployments/about-security-hardening-with-openid-connect)

GitHub Actions in a GitHub organization that isn't one of the entity's can assume this role. That organization's members, and anyone who gets write access to its repositories, get the role's access to your Alibaba Cloud account.

**How to fix**

1. If the organization is yours, add it to this entity in Keelson.
2. If it belongs to a vendor, confirm they still need the role and limit it to the repository and branch they use.
3. Otherwise remove it from the role's trust policy.

#### XP-023: Anyone who can push to the repository can assume this RAM role

**Severity:** High · **Attack path** · **Spans providers** · **Reads:** RAM roles and their trust policies · [GitHub docs](https://docs.github.com/en/actions/security-for-github-actions/security-hardening-your-deployments/about-security-hardening-with-openid-connect#example-subject-claims)

The role trusts GitHub Actions from a repository in the entity, either from any branch or pull request, or from a default branch that takes changes without review. Anyone with write access, or a stolen token or deploy key that has it, can push a workflow and act as the role in Alibaba Cloud.

**How to fix**

1. Limit the trust policy's oidc:sub to the protected default branch (repo:org/repo:ref:refs/heads/main) or, better, to a GitHub environment with required reviewers (repo:org/repo:environment:production).
2. Require a reviewed pull request on that branch in GitHub.

#### LOS-004: Bucket policy lets an Alibaba Cloud account outside the entity in

**Severity:** Medium · **Reads:** OSS bucket policies (reduced to who they allow, never stored) · [Alibaba Cloud docs](https://www.alibabacloud.com/help/en/oss/user-guide/oss-bucket-policy)

The bucket's policy grants another Alibaba Cloud account access. If it isn't one of yours, that company, and anyone who gets into its account, can reach the bucket.

**How to fix**

1. If the account is yours, add it to this entity in Keelson.
2. Otherwise edit the bucket's policy in OSS → Permission Control → Bucket Policy and remove the account, or limit it to the paths and actions it needs.

#### LEC-007: Internet-facing instance runs with administrator access

**Severity:** High · **Attack path** · **Reads:** ECS instances, Security groups and their rules, RAM roles and their trust policies, RAM policies and who they're attached to (documents reduced to what they allow, never stored) · [Alibaba Cloud docs](https://www.alibabacloud.com/help/en/ecs/user-guide/attach-an-instance-ram-role-to-an-ecs-instance)

The instance has a public address, its security group lets the internet in, and its RAM role is an administrator. A vulnerability in anything it serves can be turned into the role's credentials, and so into the whole account.

**How to fix**

1. Give the instance a role with only the permissions its software needs.
2. Require tokens for its metadata service (Security Hardening Mode).
3. Put it behind a load balancer and remove its public address.

#### LDB-004: Tair or MongoDB lets clients in the VPC connect without a password

**Severity:** High · **Attack path** · **Reads:** Tair (Redis) instances: endpoints, whitelists, password-free access and TLS, ApsaraDB for MongoDB instances: endpoints, whitelists, password-free access and TLS · [Alibaba Cloud docs](https://www.alibabacloud.com/help/en/redis/user-guide/enable-password-free-access)

Password-free access is on: any client in the VPC whose address the whitelist admits can read and change every key or document without credentials. One compromised instance, container or function in the VPC is then the whole data store, with nothing in its logs to tell an attacker from the application.

**How to fix**

In the instance's console → Instance Information (Tair) or Database Connections (MongoDB), turn password-free access off and give each application its own account with only the permissions it needs. Narrow the whitelist to the applications' addresses.

### Alibaba Cloud: Secrets

#### LEC-004: Credential in an instance's start-up script

**Severity:** High · **Reads:** Instance start-up scripts (scanned for credentials, never stored), ECS instances · [Alibaba Cloud docs](https://www.alibabacloud.com/help/en/ecs/user-guide/customize-the-initialization-configuration-for-an-instance)

User data is readable by anyone who can describe the instance, and from inside the instance through the metadata service. A token or key written into it is shared with everyone who has either.

**How to fix**

1. Rotate the credential.
2. Store it in KMS Secrets Manager and have the script fetch it at boot with the instance's RAM role.
3. Replace the user data (the instance must be stopped to change it).

#### LEC-006: Credential in a launch template's start-up script

**Severity:** High · **Reads:** ECS launch templates (start-up scripts scanned for credentials, never stored) · [Alibaba Cloud docs](https://www.alibabacloud.com/help/en/ecs/user-guide/customize-the-initialization-configuration-for-an-instance)

The template's user data is readable by anyone who can describe launch templates, and every instance launched from it carries the credential in its metadata.

**How to fix**

1. Rotate the credential.
2. Store it in KMS Secrets Manager and fetch it at boot with the instance's RAM role.
3. Create a new template version without it, make that the default, and delete the old versions.

#### LCN-002: Credential in a function's environment variables

**Severity:** High · **Reads:** Function Compute functions and triggers (environment variables scanned for credentials, never stored) · [Alibaba Cloud docs](https://www.alibabacloud.com/help/en/functioncompute/fc-3-0/user-guide/environment-variables)

Environment variables are readable by anyone who can view the function's configuration, and travel with every copy of it. A token or key there is shared with all of them.

**How to fix**

1. Rotate the credential.
2. Store it in KMS Secrets Manager and read it at run time with the function's RAM role.
3. Remove the variable from the function.

#### LIM-004: Credential stored inside an image

**Severity:** High · **Reads:** Container Registry Enterprise Edition instances, their repositories and image tags, Pulling images from Container Registry, for Trivy to scan, Packages, vulnerabilities and stored credentials in container images (Aqua Trivy) · [Alibaba Cloud docs](https://www.alibabacloud.com/help/en/acr/user-guide/scan-container-images)

Anyone who can pull the image can read the credential, from every copy of the image in every registry and cache, for as long as those exist. Deleting the file in a later layer doesn't remove it from the earlier one.

**How to fix**

1. Rotate the credential: treat it as leaked.
2. Remove it from the build: pass secrets at run time (the platform's secret store) or with a build secret mount, and add the file to .dockerignore.
3. Rebuild, deploy, and delete the old image tags.

#### LKM-001: KMS key doesn't rotate automatically

**Severity:** Low · **Reads:** KMS keys and secrets (names and dates, never values) · [Alibaba Cloud docs](https://www.alibabacloud.com/help/en/kms/key-management-service/user-guide/configure-key-rotation)

A key that never rotates protects everything encrypted with it with the same material for as long as it lives. Automatic rotation limits how much data one compromised version can expose.

**How to fix**

In the KMS console → Keys → the key → Configure Rotation, turn on automatic rotation (every 365 days or sooner).

#### LKM-003: Secret hasn't changed in over a year

**Severity:** Low · **Reads:** KMS keys and secrets (names and dates, never values) · [Alibaba Cloud docs](https://www.alibabacloud.com/help/en/kms/user-guide/overview-9)

A credential that never changes stays useful to anyone who copied it, from a log, a laptop or a former colleague, for as long as it lives.

**How to fix**

Turn on automatic rotation for the secret in KMS → Secrets (RAM, RDS and ECS secrets rotate on their own), or rotate it by hand and put a date on the next rotation.

### Alibaba Cloud: TLS & HTTPS

#### LDB-002: Database accepts connections without TLS

**Severity:** Medium · **Reads:** ApsaraDB RDS instances, their whitelists, TLS and encryption · [Alibaba Cloud docs](https://www.alibabacloud.com/help/en/rds/apsaradb-rds-for-mysql/configure-ssl-encryption-for-an-apsaradb-rds-for-mysql-instance)

Without TLS, credentials and query results cross the network in plain text. Over a public endpoint that is the internet; inside a VPC it is readable by anything on the path between the application and the database.

**How to fix**

In the instance's console → Data Security (RDS) or TLS Settings (Tair, MongoDB), turn on TLS for the endpoint the applications use, then have the clients connect with TLS.

#### LLB-001: Load balancer serves plain HTTP

**Severity:** Medium · **Reads:** Load balancers (ALB, NLB, CLB) and listeners · [Alibaba Cloud docs](https://www.alibabacloud.com/help/en/slb/application-load-balancer/use-cases/redirect-http-requests-to-an-https-listener)

The internet-facing load balancer answers on HTTP without sending visitors to HTTPS, so their requests and cookies cross the network unencrypted.

**How to fix**

In the SLB console → the load balancer → Listener, change the HTTP listener to redirect to the HTTPS listener (ALB: a redirect forwarding rule; CLB: Redirect HTTP to HTTPS).

#### LLB-002: Load balancer accepts TLS 1.0 or 1.1

**Severity:** Medium · **Reads:** Load balancers (ALB, NLB, CLB) and listeners · [Alibaba Cloud docs](https://www.alibabacloud.com/help/en/slb/application-load-balancer/user-guide/tls-security-policies)

The listener's TLS security policy still negotiates TLS 1.0 or 1.1, which have known weaknesses and fail PCI DSS.

**How to fix**

In the SLB console → the load balancer → Listener, edit the HTTPS listener and choose tls_cipher_policy_1_2_strict_with_1_3, or tls_cipher_policy_1_2 if old clients must connect.

#### LLB-003: CDN domain serves only plain HTTP

**Severity:** Medium · **Reads:** CDN domains · [Alibaba Cloud docs](https://www.alibabacloud.com/help/en/cdn/user-guide/configure-an-ssl-certificate)

The accelerated domain has no HTTPS certificate, so visitors' requests, cookies and the content they get cross the network unencrypted and can be read or changed on the way.

**How to fix**

In the CDN console → Domain Names → the domain → HTTPS, add a certificate (a free one from Certificate Management Service works), then turn on Force HTTPS redirect.

### Alibaba Cloud: WAF & bots

#### XP-018: Alibaba Cloud origin behind Cloudflare accepts traffic from the whole internet

**Severity:** High · **Attack path** · **Spans providers** · **Reads:** Load balancers (ALB, NLB, CLB) and listeners, Security groups and their rules, Network interfaces and EIPs · [Cloudflare docs](https://developers.cloudflare.com/fundamentals/security/protect-your-origin-server/)

Visitors reach this origin through Cloudflare, where your WAF, rate limits and bot rules run. Its security group also lets anyone connect to it directly, and origin addresses are easy to find (certificate logs, old DNS records, internet scans). An attacker who connects directly skips every Cloudflare protection and can flood the origin itself.

**How to fix**

1. In the security group, replace 0.0.0.0/0 on ports 80 and 443 with Cloudflare's address ranges (cloudflare.com/ips); a prefix list keeps them in one place.
2. Or connect the origin through Cloudflare Tunnel and remove the inbound rule altogether.
3. Turn on Authenticated Origin Pulls in Cloudflare so the origin can refuse requests that didn't come through your zone.

### Alibaba Cloud: DNS

#### LDN-001: Alibaba Cloud DNS record points at an Alibaba Cloud resource the entity doesn't have

**Severity:** Medium · **Attack path** · **Reads:** Alibaba Cloud DNS domains and records, OSS buckets, Load balancers (ALB, NLB, CLB) and listeners, CDN domains · [Alibaba Cloud docs](https://www.alibabacloud.com/help/en/dns/add-a-dns-record)

The record names an OSS bucket, load balancer or CDN domain that none of the entity's Alibaba Cloud accounts has. A deleted bucket's name can be registered by anyone; OSS won't serve your hostname from it without proof that they own the domain, but links to the bucket's own address would load their files. A missing load balancer or CDN domain can't be claimed that way, so that record is dead, or points into an account Keelson doesn't see.

**How to fix**

1. If the site was retired, delete the record in Alibaba Cloud DNS.
2. If it should be live, recreate the resource or point the record at the current one.
3. If the resource belongs to an Alibaba Cloud account that isn't in Keelson, add that account to this entity, or mark the finding as a false positive.

#### LDN-002: Alibaba Cloud DNS record points at an address the entity released

**Severity:** High · **Attack path** · **Reads:** Alibaba Cloud DNS domains and records, Network interfaces and EIPs · [Alibaba Cloud docs](https://www.alibabacloud.com/help/en/dns/add-a-dns-record)

Keelson saw this address in one of the entity's Alibaba Cloud accounts on an earlier scan, and it is gone now: the instance was released or the EIP was given back. Alibaba Cloud hands released addresses to other customers, and whoever gets this one receives your hostname's traffic and can obtain a certificate for it.

**How to fix**

1. If the server is gone, delete the record in Alibaba Cloud DNS.
2. If it moved, point the record at its current address, and use an EIP or a load balancer so the address can't change again.
3. If the address moved to an account that isn't in Keelson, add that account to this entity.

#### XP-019: Alibaba Cloud DNS record points at Vercel, but no Vercel project in the entity serves it

**Severity:** High · **Attack path** · **Spans providers** · **Reads:** Alibaba Cloud DNS domains and records · [Vercel docs](https://vercel.com/docs/domains/working-with-domains/add-a-domain)

The record sends visitors to Vercel, yet none of the entity's Vercel projects has this hostname. Whoever adds it to their own Vercel project first serves your traffic under your domain.

**How to fix**

1. If the site moved or was retired, delete the record in Alibaba Cloud DNS.
2. If it should be live, add the hostname to the right Vercel project under Settings → Domains.
3. If it belongs to a Vercel team that isn't in Keelson, add that team to this entity, or mark the finding as a false positive.

#### XP-020: Alibaba Cloud DNS record points at an AWS resource or address the entity doesn't have

**Severity:** High · **Attack path** · **Spans providers** · **Reads:** Alibaba Cloud DNS domains and records · [AWS docs](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/Route53/latest/DeveloperGuide/protection-from-dangling-dns.html)

The record names a CloudFront distribution, load balancer or S3 bucket that none of the entity's AWS accounts has, or an address Keelson saw leave them. A missing bucket or CloudFront alias can be claimed by anyone, and a released address is handed to another AWS customer; either way someone else can serve your hostname.

**How to fix**

1. If the site moved or was retired, delete the record in Alibaba Cloud DNS.
2. If it should be live, recreate the resource or point the record at the current one.
3. If the resource belongs to an AWS account that isn't in Keelson, add that account to this entity.

#### XP-024: Alibaba Cloud DNS record points at GitHub Pages, but no repository in the entity publishes it

**Severity:** High · **Attack path** · **Spans providers** · **Reads:** Alibaba Cloud DNS domains and records · [GitHub docs](https://docs.github.com/en/pages/configuring-a-custom-domain-for-your-github-pages-site/verifying-your-custom-domain-for-github-pages)

The record sends visitors to GitHub Pages, yet none of the entity's GitHub organizations has a Pages site with this custom domain. Anyone can add the hostname to a Pages site of their own and serve content under your domain, unless the domain is verified in GitHub.

**How to fix**

1. If the site was retired, delete the record in Alibaba Cloud DNS.
2. If it should be live, set the custom domain on the right repository's Pages settings.
3. Verify the domain in your GitHub organization's settings so no one else can use it.
4. If the site belongs to an organization that isn't in Keelson, add it to this entity.

### Alibaba Cloud: Platform

#### LEC-001: Instance's metadata service answers without a token

**Severity:** Medium · **Reads:** ECS instances · [Alibaba Cloud docs](https://www.alibabacloud.com/help/en/ecs/user-guide/view-instance-metadata)

In normal mode the metadata service answers any request from the instance, so a server-side request forgery in the application is enough to read the temporary credentials of the instance's RAM role. Security hardening mode requires a token that such a request can't get.

**How to fix**

In the ECS console, open the instance → Modify Instance Metadata Access Mode and choose Security Hardening Mode (tokens required), after checking that the software on it uses a current SDK or Cloud Assistant.

#### LEC-002: Cloud disks aren't encrypted by default

**Severity:** Low · **Reads:** Cloud disks and encryption by default, ECS instances · [Alibaba Cloud docs](https://www.alibabacloud.com/help/en/ecs/user-guide/encryption-overview)

Unlike some clouds, Alibaba Cloud doesn't encrypt ECS disks unless asked. New disks, and every snapshot and image made from them, are stored unencrypted unless whoever creates them remembers to ask, and a snapshot shared or copied by mistake carries the data in the clear. Encryption by default makes every new disk encrypted with no change to how instances use it.

**How to fix**

1. In the ECS console → Block Storage → Cloud Disks, turn on Account-level Encryption by Default for the region.
2. Existing disks stay as they are: re-create the ones holding sensitive data from an encrypted snapshot copy during a maintenance window.

#### LEC-005: Launch template lets instances answer metadata requests without a token

**Severity:** Medium · **Reads:** ECS launch templates (start-up scripts scanned for credentials, never stored) · [Alibaba Cloud docs](https://www.alibabacloud.com/help/en/ecs/user-guide/view-instance-metadata)

Every instance launched from this template, by a scaling group or by hand, starts in normal mode, where a server-side request forgery can read its RAM role's credentials.

**How to fix**

Create a new version of the template with Security Hardening Mode for the metadata service, and make it the default version.

#### LDB-003: Database storage isn't encrypted

**Severity:** Low · **Reads:** ApsaraDB RDS instances, their whitelists, TLS and encryption · [Alibaba Cloud docs](https://www.alibabacloud.com/help/en/rds/apsaradb-rds-for-mysql/configure-tde-for-an-apsaradb-rds-for-mysql-instance)

Transparent data encryption is off, so the database's files and backups are stored unencrypted, and a copied backup carries the data in the clear. Access to the instance itself matters more: this is the last line, not the first.

**How to fix**

In the RDS console → the instance → Data Security → TDE, turn on TDE with a KMS key. It can't be turned off again, so check the engine version's notes first.

### Alibaba Cloud: Supply chain

#### LIM-001: Image in use has a vulnerability attackers are exploiting

**Severity:** Critical · **Attack path** · **Reads:** Container Registry Enterprise Edition instances, their repositories and image tags, Pulling images from Container Registry, for Trivy to scan, Packages, vulnerabilities and stored credentials in container images (Aqua Trivy), CISA's catalog of known exploited vulnerabilities · [Alibaba Cloud docs](https://www.alibabacloud.com/help/en/acr/user-guide/scan-container-images)

A package in the image has a vulnerability on CISA's list of known exploited vulnerabilities (cisa.gov/known-exploited-vulnerabilities-catalog), and something runs the image. Attackers already have working exploits for it, and a service the internet reaches is where they try them first.

**How to fix**

1. Rebuild the image with the fixed versions: update the base image for operating system packages, and the lock file for the application's own dependencies (the Images page says which is which).
2. Push it and deploy the workloads that run it.
3. Where there is no fix yet, limit who can reach the workload until there is.

#### LIM-002: Image in use has critical or high vulnerabilities with a fix

**Severity:** High · **Reads:** Container Registry Enterprise Edition instances, their repositories and image tags, Pulling images from Container Registry, for Trivy to scan, Packages, vulnerabilities and stored credentials in container images (Aqua Trivy) · [Alibaba Cloud docs](https://www.alibabacloud.com/help/en/acr/user-guide/scan-container-images)

The image runs with packages that have known critical or high vulnerabilities, and fixed versions exist. Each rebuild that doesn't pick them up leaves a known way in for longer.

**How to fix**

1. Rebuild the image with the fixed versions: update the base image for operating system packages, and the lock file for the application's own dependencies (the Images page says which is which).
2. Push it and deploy the workloads that run it.
3. Where there is no fix yet, limit who can reach the workload until there is.

#### LIM-003: Image in use is built on an operating system or runtime past its end of life

**Severity:** Medium · **Reads:** Container Registry Enterprise Edition instances, their repositories and image tags, Pulling images from Container Registry, for Trivy to scan, Packages, vulnerabilities and stored credentials in container images (Aqua Trivy) · [Alibaba Cloud docs](https://www.alibabacloud.com/help/en/acr/user-guide/scan-container-images)

The operating system release in the image, or the release line of the runtime it is built around (Node.js, Python, nginx…), no longer gets security fixes. Vulnerabilities found in it from now on stay open, and scanners stop reporting them for it.

**How to fix**

Change the Dockerfile's FROM line to a release that is still supported (or to the newest tag of the same base image), rebuild, test and deploy.

### Alibaba Cloud: Monitoring

#### LMO-001: ActionTrail doesn't record every region

**Severity:** High · **Reads:** ActionTrail trails · [Alibaba Cloud docs](https://www.alibabacloud.com/help/en/actiontrail/user-guide/create-a-single-account-trail)

Without a trail that records reads and writes in every region and delivers them to OSS or Log Service, the account keeps only 90 days of events in the console, and nothing at all an investigator can query after that. A break-in would leave no lasting record of what was done.

**How to fix**

In the ActionTrail console → Trails → Create Trail, choose All Regions and All event types (Read and Write), and deliver the events to a private OSS bucket or a Log Service project. Keep the trail turned on.

#### LMO-002: VPC with running resources has no flow logs

**Severity:** Low · **Reads:** VPCs and flow logs, ECS instances, ApsaraDB RDS instances, their whitelists, TLS and encryption, Load balancers (ALB, NLB, CLB) and listeners · [Alibaba Cloud docs](https://www.alibabacloud.com/help/en/vpc/user-guide/flow-logs)

Without flow logs, nobody can tell after the fact which addresses talked to what in the VPC: an investigation has no record of connections in or out.

**How to fix**

In the VPC console → Flow Logs, create a flow log for the VPC (or its vSwitches) that delivers to Log Service.

#### LMO-003: Running instance isn't protected by Security Center's agent

**Severity:** Low · **Reads:** Security Center agents, ECS instances · [Alibaba Cloud docs](https://www.alibabacloud.com/help/en/security-center/user-guide/install-the-security-center-agent)

Security Center's agent, included for free, detects brute-force logins, web shells and known vulnerabilities on the instance. Without it, a compromise of this server raises no alert.

**How to fix**

In the Security Center console → Assets → Servers, install the agent on the instance (one click for ECS), or with Cloud Assistant across many instances.

### Alibaba Cloud: Change risk

#### LKM-002: KMS key is scheduled for deletion

**Severity:** Medium · **Reads:** KMS keys and secrets (names and dates, never values) · [Alibaba Cloud docs](https://www.alibabacloud.com/help/en/kms/key-management-service/user-guide/manage-keys-2)

Once the waiting period ends, data encrypted with the key can never be decrypted again: disks, databases, OSS objects and secrets that use it are lost.

**How to fix**

If anything still uses the key, cancel the deletion in the KMS console → Keys → the key → Cancel Deletion. Otherwise let it go, and note who scheduled it.

## GitHub

### GitHub: Identity & access

#### GID-001: Organization doesn't require two-factor authentication

**Severity:** High · **Attack path** · **Reads:** Organization settings · [GitHub docs](https://docs.github.com/en/organizations/keeping-your-organization-secure/managing-two-factor-authentication-for-your-organization/requiring-two-factor-authentication-in-your-organization)

Members can sign in with a password alone. A phished or reused password then gives someone your code, your Actions secrets and whatever those workflows deploy to.

**How to fix**

1. Open the organization's Settings → Authentication security.
2. Tick Require two-factor authentication for everyone. Members without it are removed until they set it up, so tell them first.

#### GID-002: Every member can change every repository

**Severity:** Medium · **Reads:** Organization settings · [GitHub docs](https://docs.github.com/en/organizations/managing-user-access-to-your-organizations-repositories/managing-repository-roles/setting-base-permissions-for-an-organization)

The base permission is Write or Admin, so every member can push to every repository, including ones they have nothing to do with. One stolen login reaches all of your code.

**How to fix**

Under Settings → Member privileges, set Base permissions to Read or No permission, and give teams write access to the repositories they work on.

#### GID-003: Members can create public repositories

**Severity:** Low · **Reads:** Organization settings · [GitHub docs](https://docs.github.com/en/organizations/managing-organization-settings/restricting-repository-creation-in-your-organization)

Anyone in the organization can publish code under its name, and a repository meant to be private can be created public by mistake.

**How to fix**

Under Settings → Member privileges → Repository creation, untick Public. Owners can still create public repositories.

#### GID-004: Too many organization owners

**Severity:** Medium · **Reads:** Organization owners · [GitHub docs](https://docs.github.com/en/organizations/managing-peoples-access-to-your-organization-with-roles/roles-in-an-organization)

Every owner can change any setting, delete repositories, read every secret's name and add Apps with access to all code. Each extra owner widens what a stolen login can do.

**How to fix**

Keep two or three owners for break-glass access. Under People, change everyone else's role to Member and give their teams the access they need.

#### GID-005: Members can fork private repositories

**Severity:** Low · **Reads:** Organization settings · [GitHub docs](https://docs.github.com/en/organizations/managing-organization-settings/managing-the-forking-policy-for-your-organization)

A fork of a private repository can live in a personal account, outside the organization's settings, and stays with the person after they leave.

**How to fix**

Under Settings → Member privileges, untick Allow forking of private repositories, or allow it only within the organization where your plan offers that.

#### GID-006: Members can make private repositories public

**Severity:** Medium · **Reads:** Organization settings · [GitHub docs](https://docs.github.com/en/organizations/managing-organization-settings/restricting-repository-visibility-changes-in-your-organization)

A member with admin access to a repository can make it public in two clicks, publishing its code and its whole history, including any secret ever committed. Only owners should be able to do that.

**How to fix**

Under the organization's Settings → Member privileges → Repository visibility change, untick Allow members to change repository visibilities for this organization.

#### GID-007: Members can delete or transfer repositories

**Severity:** Low · **Reads:** Organization settings · [GitHub docs](https://docs.github.com/en/organizations/managing-organization-settings/setting-permissions-for-deleting-or-transferring-repositories)

A member with admin access to a repository, or someone with their login, can delete it or transfer it to an account outside the organization, taking the code, issues and settings with it.

**How to fix**

Under the organization's Settings → Member privileges → Repository deletion and transfer, untick Allow members to delete or transfer repositories for this organization.

#### GHK-003: Deploy key can push to the repository

**Severity:** Medium · **Reads:** Deploy keys · [GitHub docs](https://docs.github.com/en/authentication/connecting-to-github-with-ssh/managing-deploy-keys#deploy-keys)

A deploy key with write access isn't tied to a person, doesn't expire and isn't covered by two-factor authentication. Whoever holds the private key can push, and it usually sits on a server.

**How to fix**

In the repository's Settings → Deploy keys, remove the key and add it again without Allow write access, or replace it with a GitHub App that has only the access it needs.

#### GHK-004: GitHub App can change every repository

**Severity:** Medium · **Reads:** Installed GitHub Apps · [GitHub docs](https://docs.github.com/en/apps/using-github-apps/reviewing-and-modifying-installed-github-apps)

The App can write code, workflows or settings in every repository, including ones created later. If the vendor or its keys are compromised, so is all of your code.

**How to fix**

Under the organization's Settings → GitHub Apps, open the App's Configure page and choose Only select repositories, or remove it if nobody uses it.

### GitHub: Deployments

#### GAC-001: Workflows get a token that can write by default

**Severity:** Medium · **Reads:** Actions permissions · [GitHub docs](https://docs.github.com/en/actions/security-for-github-actions/security-guides/automatic-token-authentication#modifying-the-permissions-for-the-github_token)

Every workflow run gets a GITHUB_TOKEN that can push code, create releases and change issues, even when it only builds or tests. A compromised action or a script injection then changes the repository.

**How to fix**

Under the organization's Settings → Actions → General → Workflow permissions, choose Read repository contents and packages permissions. Give a workflow more with a permissions block where it needs it.

#### GAC-002: Workflows can approve pull requests

**Severity:** Medium · **Reads:** Actions permissions · [GitHub docs](https://docs.github.com/en/organizations/managing-organization-settings/disabling-or-limiting-github-actions-for-your-organization#preventing-github-actions-from-creating-or-approving-pull-requests)

A workflow can approve a pull request, including one it opened. That satisfies a required review with no person involved, so the review rule protects nothing against a compromised workflow.

**How to fix**

Under the organization's Settings → Actions → General → Workflow permissions, untick Allow GitHub Actions to create and approve pull requests.

#### GAC-003: Any third-party action can run

**Severity:** Low · **Reads:** Actions permissions · [GitHub docs](https://docs.github.com/en/organizations/managing-organization-settings/disabling-or-limiting-github-actions-for-your-organization#allowing-select-actions-and-reusable-workflows-to-run)

Workflows can use any action from any author. An action runs with the workflow's token and secrets, so one compromised action reaches every repository that uses it.

**How to fix**

Under the organization's Settings → Actions → General → Policies, choose Allow enterprise, and select non-enterprise, actions and reusable workflows. Allow actions created by GitHub, verified creators and the ones you name.

#### GAC-004: Pull requests from forks of private repositories get secrets or a write token

**Severity:** High · **Attack path** · **Reads:** Workflow policy for fork pull requests · [GitHub docs](https://docs.github.com/en/organizations/managing-organization-settings/disabling-or-limiting-github-actions-for-your-organization#enabling-workflows-for-private-repository-forks)

A workflow started by a pull request from a fork runs the fork's version of the workflow. Anyone who can fork a private repository can then read every secret the workflow can reach, or use its token to change the repository, before anyone reviews the change.

**How to fix**

Under the organization's Settings → Actions → General, in the section for forks of private repositories, untick Send write tokens to workflows from pull requests and Send secrets to workflows from pull requests. If fork pull requests must run workflows, also tick Require approval for fork pull request workflows.

#### GAC-005: Public repository can run jobs on self-hosted runners

**Severity:** High · **Attack path** · **Reads:** Self-hosted runners and runner groups, Public repositories' own self-hosted runners · [GitHub docs](https://docs.github.com/en/actions/hosting-your-own-runners/managing-self-hosted-runners/about-self-hosted-runners#self-hosted-runner-security)

A pull request to a public repository can change its workflows to run anything on your own machines, which sit inside your network with whatever credentials they hold. A runner that isn't ephemeral also keeps what the job left behind for the next job, including a backdoor.

**How to fix**

1. Move the runners into a runner group that public repositories can't use: under the organization's Settings → Actions → Runner groups, untick Allow public repositories.
2. Remove runners added to the public repository itself, under its Settings → Actions → Runners.
3. If a public repository needs them, use ephemeral runners, limit the group to named workflows, and under Settings → Actions → General choose Require approval for all external contributors.

### GitHub: Secrets

#### GSC-001: Public repository doesn't scan for leaked secrets

**Severity:** High · **Reads:** Code security settings · [GitHub docs](https://docs.github.com/en/code-security/secret-scanning/enabling-secret-scanning-features/enabling-secret-scanning-for-your-repository)

Anyone can read a public repository and its whole history. Secret scanning is free there and tells you when a key or token is committed, often before someone else finds it.

**How to fix**

In the repository's Settings → Code security, enable Secret scanning. To cover every public repository, apply a security configuration under the organization's Settings → Code security → Configurations.

#### GSC-002: Push protection is off

**Severity:** Medium · **Reads:** Code security settings · [GitHub docs](https://docs.github.com/en/code-security/secret-scanning/protecting-pushes-with-secret-scanning)

Secret scanning only reports a secret after it's pushed, when it's already in the history. Push protection stops the push instead.

**How to fix**

In the repository's Settings → Code security, enable Push protection under Secret scanning, or turn it on in the organization's security configuration.

#### GSC-003: Leaked secret found in a repository and not resolved

**Severity:** Critical · **Attack path** · **Reads:** Secret scanning alerts · [GitHub docs](https://docs.github.com/en/code-security/secret-scanning/managing-alerts-from-secret-scanning/resolving-alerts-from-secret-scanning)

GitHub found a credential in the code or its history. Anyone who can read the repository, or who cloned it before, can use it until it's revoked.

**How to fix**

1. Revoke or rotate the credential where it was issued. Deleting the commit doesn't help: the value stays in clones and forks.
2. Close the alert in the repository's Security → Secret scanning as Revoked.

#### GIM-004: Credential stored inside an image

**Severity:** High · **Reads:** Container packages in GitHub Container Registry, and their tags, Packages, vulnerabilities and stored credentials in public container images (Aqua Trivy) · [GitHub docs](https://docs.github.com/en/packages/working-with-a-github-packages-registry/working-with-the-container-registry)

Anyone who can pull the image can read the credential, from every copy of the image in every registry and cache, for as long as those exist. Deleting the file in a later layer doesn't remove it from the earlier one.

**How to fix**

1. Rotate the credential: treat it as leaked.
2. Remove it from the build: pass secrets at run time (the platform's secret store) or with a build secret mount, and add the file to .dockerignore.
3. Rebuild, deploy, and delete the old image tags.

### GitHub: TLS & HTTPS

#### GHK-001: Webhook doesn't verify the receiver's certificate

**Severity:** Medium · **Reads:** Organization webhooks, Repository webhooks · [GitHub docs](https://docs.github.com/en/webhooks/using-webhooks/creating-webhooks)

SSL verification is off, so anyone who can intercept the traffic can pose as the receiver and read every event GitHub sends, including code changes and who made them.

**How to fix**

Open the webhook in Settings → Webhooks, choose Enable SSL verification, and give the receiver a valid certificate.

#### GHK-002: Webhook sends events over plain HTTP

**Severity:** Medium · **Reads:** Organization webhooks, Repository webhooks · [GitHub docs](https://docs.github.com/en/webhooks/using-webhooks/best-practices-for-using-webhooks)

Events, with commit messages, branch names and who pushed what, cross the internet unencrypted, and the signature header can be replayed.

**How to fix**

Change the webhook's Payload URL to https:// and make sure the receiver serves HTTPS.

#### GPG-001: GitHub Pages site doesn't enforce HTTPS

**Severity:** Low · **Reads:** GitHub Pages sites · [GitHub docs](https://docs.github.com/en/pages/getting-started-with-github-pages/securing-your-github-pages-site-with-https)

Visitors who type the address or follow an old http:// link get the site unencrypted, where anyone on the network can change it.

**How to fix**

In the repository's Settings → Pages, tick Enforce HTTPS. GitHub offers it once the custom domain's certificate is issued.

### GitHub: Platform

#### GSC-005: Code scanning found a critical or high vulnerability

**Severity:** High · **Reads:** Code scanning alerts, Whether code scanning has run · [GitHub docs](https://docs.github.com/en/code-security/code-scanning/managing-code-scanning-alerts/assessing-code-scanning-alerts-for-your-repository)

Code scanning found a weakness in the repository's own code rated critical or high, such as an injection or a path traversal.

**How to fix**

Open the repository's Security → Code scanning, fix the code it points at, or dismiss the alert with the reason when it's a false positive.

#### GSC-006: Dependabot security updates are off where Dependabot has found something

**Severity:** Low · **Reads:** Code security settings, Dependabot alerts · [GitHub docs](https://docs.github.com/en/code-security/dependabot/dependabot-security-updates/configuring-dependabot-security-updates)

The repository has open Dependabot alerts, and without security updates each fix waits for someone to notice the alert and make the change by hand.

**How to fix**

In the repository's Settings → Code security, enable Dependabot security updates, or turn it on in the organization's security configuration. Dependabot then opens a pull request for each fix.

#### GSC-007: Dependabot alerts are off

**Severity:** Medium · **Reads:** Whether Dependabot alerts are on · [GitHub docs](https://docs.github.com/en/code-security/dependabot/dependabot-alerts/configuring-dependabot-alerts)

GitHub doesn't tell anyone when a dependency of this repository has a published vulnerability. Dependabot alerts are free on every repository, private ones included.

**How to fix**

In the repository's Settings → Code security, enable Dependabot alerts. To cover every repository, apply a security configuration under the organization's Settings → Code security → Configurations.

#### GSC-008: Public repository isn't scanned for vulnerabilities in its code

**Severity:** Medium · **Reads:** Whether code scanning has run · [GitHub docs](https://docs.github.com/en/code-security/code-scanning/enabling-code-scanning/configuring-default-setup-for-code-scanning)

Anyone can read this code and look for injections and other weaknesses in it. Code scanning is free on public repositories and finds many of them first.

**How to fix**

In the repository's Settings → Code security, choose Set up → Default under Code scanning, or turn it on for every public repository in the organization's security configuration.

### GitHub: Supply chain

#### GSC-004: Dependency with a critical or high vulnerability

**Severity:** High · **Reads:** Dependabot alerts, Whether Dependabot alerts are on · [GitHub docs](https://docs.github.com/en/code-security/dependabot/dependabot-alerts/viewing-and-updating-dependabot-alerts)

A package the repository depends on has a published vulnerability rated critical or high, so how to exploit it is public.

**How to fix**

Open the repository's Security → Dependabot alerts, update the packages, or dismiss an alert with the reason when the vulnerable code isn't reachable.

#### GDP-001: Dependency has a vulnerability attackers are exploiting

**Severity:** Critical · **Attack path** · **Reads:** Manifest and lock files, for each repository's SBOM (never the code), Software bill of materials (Anchore Syft), Known vulnerabilities in dependencies (Anchore Grype) · [GitHub docs](https://docs.github.com/en/code-security/supply-chain-security/understanding-your-software-supply-chain/about-supply-chain-security)

A package this repository uses has a vulnerability in CISA's catalog of known exploited vulnerabilities: attackers are using it now, with tools that are already public. Anything built from this code that runs the package is exposed.

**How to fix**

1. Upgrade the package to the version the evidence names, in every part that uses it, and deploy.
2. If it comes in through another package, upgrade that one, or override the version (npm overrides, Yarn resolutions, a Go replace or a constraint).
3. Check what ran it before the upgrade for signs of compromise.

#### GDP-002: Dependency has a critical or high vulnerability

**Severity:** High · **Reads:** Manifest and lock files, for each repository's SBOM (never the code), Software bill of materials (Anchore Syft), Known vulnerabilities in dependencies (Anchore Grype) · [GitHub docs](https://docs.github.com/en/code-security/supply-chain-security/understanding-your-software-supply-chain/about-supply-chain-security)

A package this repository uses has a published vulnerability rated critical or high, or one that FIRST's EPSS rates likely to be exploited soon. How to exploit it is public, so whatever is built from this code inherits it until the package is upgraded.

**How to fix**

1. Upgrade the package to the version the evidence names; it fixes every listed vulnerability that has a fix.
2. If it comes in through another package, upgrade that one, or override the version (npm overrides, Yarn resolutions, a Go replace or a constraint).
3. If the vulnerable code can't be reached from how you use it, mark the finding as accepted with the reason.

#### GDP-003: Dependency is a known malicious package

**Severity:** Critical · **Attack path** · **Reads:** Manifest and lock files, for each repository's SBOM (never the code), Software bill of materials (Anchore Syft), Known vulnerabilities in dependencies (Anchore Grype) · [GitHub docs](https://docs.github.com/en/code-security/security-advisories/working-with-global-security-advisories-from-the-github-advisory-database/about-the-github-advisory-database)

The package is listed as malware: published to steal credentials, open a backdoor or run code when it's installed. Installing it is enough, so every developer machine and CI runner that installed this version may be compromised.

**How to fix**

1. Remove the package, or move to a version that isn't listed, and regenerate the lock file.
2. Treat every machine and CI runner that installed it as compromised: rotate the credentials they held.
3. Check how it got in: a typo in the name, or a dependency that pulled it.

#### GDP-004: Workflows run third-party actions by a tag that can be moved

**Severity:** Low · **Reads:** Manifest and lock files, for each repository's SBOM (never the code) · [GitHub docs](https://docs.github.com/en/actions/security-for-github-actions/security-guides/security-hardening-for-github-actions#using-third-party-actions)

A tag such as v4 can be pointed at different code at any time, by the action's owner or by whoever takes over their account. Workflows run that code with the repository's token and secrets, as happened with tj-actions/changed-files in 2025. A commit SHA can't be moved.

**How to fix**

Pin each third-party action to the full commit SHA of the release you use, with the tag in a comment (uses: owner/action@<sha> # v4). Dependabot or Renovate keep pinned actions up to date. Actions owned by GitHub (actions/*, github/*) and your own organization aren't counted.

#### GDP-005: Project installs dependencies without a lock file

**Severity:** Low · **Reads:** Manifest and lock files, for each repository's SBOM (never the code) · [GitHub docs](https://docs.github.com/en/code-security/supply-chain-security/understanding-your-software-supply-chain/dependency-graph-supported-package-ecosystems)

Without a lock file, or with version ranges in a requirements file, every install takes whatever version is newest at that moment. A malicious or broken release reaches your builds without anyone changing the code, and Keelson can't check those versions for vulnerabilities.

**How to fix**

Commit the lock file your package manager writes (package-lock.json, yarn.lock, pnpm-lock.yaml, go.sum, Gemfile.lock, composer.lock, poetry.lock, Pipfile.lock), and install from it in CI (npm ci, pip install with pinned == versions or a lock).

#### GLI-001: Dependency under a strong copyleft license

**Severity:** Low · **Reads:** Manifest and lock files, for each repository's SBOM (never the code), Software bill of materials (Anchore Syft), Dependency licenses (Anchore Grant) · [GitHub docs](https://docs.github.com/en/repositories/managing-your-repositorys-settings-and-features/customizing-your-repository/licensing-a-repository)

The package's license (such as GPL or AGPL) requires software that includes it to be released under the same terms when it's distributed, or for AGPL and SSPL when it's offered over a network. A repository that isn't under a compatible license may have to release its own code, or remove the package.

**How to fix**

Check with whoever looks after licensing whether this use is allowed: it depends on how the software is distributed or offered. Otherwise replace the package with one under a permissive license. Mark the finding as accepted when the use is cleared.

#### GIM-001: Image in use has a vulnerability attackers are exploiting

**Severity:** Critical · **Attack path** · **Reads:** Container packages in GitHub Container Registry, and their tags, Packages, vulnerabilities and stored credentials in public container images (Aqua Trivy), CISA's catalog of known exploited vulnerabilities · [GitHub docs](https://docs.github.com/en/packages/working-with-a-github-packages-registry/working-with-the-container-registry)

A package in the image has a vulnerability on CISA's list of known exploited vulnerabilities (cisa.gov/known-exploited-vulnerabilities-catalog), and something runs the image. Attackers already have working exploits for it, and a service the internet reaches is where they try them first.

**How to fix**

1. Rebuild the image with the fixed versions: update the base image for operating system packages, and the lock file for the application's own dependencies (the Images page says which is which).
2. Push it and deploy the workloads that run it.
3. Where there is no fix yet, limit who can reach the workload until there is.

#### GIM-002: Image in use has critical or high vulnerabilities with a fix

**Severity:** High · **Reads:** Container packages in GitHub Container Registry, and their tags, Packages, vulnerabilities and stored credentials in public container images (Aqua Trivy) · [GitHub docs](https://docs.github.com/en/packages/working-with-a-github-packages-registry/working-with-the-container-registry)

The image runs with packages that have known critical or high vulnerabilities, and fixed versions exist. Each rebuild that doesn't pick them up leaves a known way in for longer.

**How to fix**

1. Rebuild the image with the fixed versions: update the base image for operating system packages, and the lock file for the application's own dependencies (the Images page says which is which).
2. Push it and deploy the workloads that run it.
3. Where there is no fix yet, limit who can reach the workload until there is.

#### GIM-003: Image in use is built on an operating system or runtime past its end of life

**Severity:** Medium · **Reads:** Container packages in GitHub Container Registry, and their tags, Packages, vulnerabilities and stored credentials in public container images (Aqua Trivy) · [GitHub docs](https://docs.github.com/en/packages/working-with-a-github-packages-registry/working-with-the-container-registry)

The operating system release in the image, or the release line of the runtime it is built around (Node.js, Python, nginx…), no longer gets security fixes. Vulnerabilities found in it from now on stay open, and scanners stop reporting them for it.

**How to fix**

Change the Dockerfile's FROM line to a release that is still supported (or to the newest tag of the same base image), rebuild, test and deploy.

### GitHub: Change risk

#### GBR-001: Default branch accepts changes without a pull request

**Severity:** Medium · **Reads:** Branch protection, Rulesets that apply to default branches · [GitHub docs](https://docs.github.com/en/repositories/configuring-branches-and-merges-in-your-repository/managing-rulesets/about-rulesets)

Anyone with write access, or a token or deploy key that has it, can push straight to the branch your releases come from, with no review and nothing in the history to stop it.

**How to fix**

1. Under the organization's Settings → Repository → Rulesets (or the repository's Settings → Rules), create a branch ruleset targeting the default branch.
2. Turn on Require a pull request before merging, with at least one approval.
3. Turn on Block force pushes and Restrict deletions.

#### GBR-002: Default branch history can be rewritten or deleted

**Severity:** Medium · **Reads:** Branch protection, Rulesets that apply to default branches · [GitHub docs](https://docs.github.com/en/repositories/configuring-branches-and-merges-in-your-repository/managing-rulesets/available-rules-for-rulesets)

The branch is protected, but a force push or deletion is still allowed. That rewrites or removes reviewed history, which also removes the evidence of what was there.

**How to fix**

In the rule or ruleset that protects the default branch, turn on Block force pushes and Restrict deletions.

#### GBR-004: An approved pull request can change before it merges

**Severity:** Medium · **Reads:** Branch protection, Rulesets that apply to default branches · [GitHub docs](https://docs.github.com/en/repositories/configuring-branches-and-merges-in-your-repository/managing-rulesets/available-rules-for-rulesets#require-a-pull-request-before-merging)

The default branch needs an approval, but the approval stays after new commits are pushed. Someone can get a harmless change approved, then push something else to the same pull request and merge it without anyone reviewing it.

**How to fix**

In the rule or ruleset that protects the default branch, turn on Dismiss stale pull request approvals when new commits are pushed. Also turn on Require approval of the most recent reviewable push, so a reviewer can't push to a pull request and approve their own change.

#### GBR-003: Administrators can skip the default branch's review rule

**Severity:** Low · **Reads:** Branch protection, Rulesets that apply to default branches · [GitHub docs](https://docs.github.com/en/repositories/configuring-branches-and-merges-in-your-repository/managing-protected-branches/about-protected-branches#do-not-allow-bypassing-the-above-settings)

Branch protection requires a pull request, but repository administrators and owners can push past it. Their logins and tokens are the ones most worth stealing.

**How to fix**

In the branch protection rule, tick Do not allow bypassing the above settings, or move the rule to a ruleset and list only who may bypass it.

#### GRL-001: Published releases can be changed

**Severity:** Medium · **Reads:** Whether public repositories publish releases, Whether releases are immutable · [GitHub docs](https://docs.github.com/en/code-security/how-tos/secure-your-supply-chain/establish-provenance-and-integrity/prevent-release-changes)

Anyone with write access, or a stolen token that has it, can replace a published release's files or point its tag at other code. Everyone who downloads that release, or uses an action pinned to that tag, then runs the new code without any sign that it changed.

**How to fix**

In the repository's Settings, under Releases, select Enable release immutability. To enforce it everywhere, under the organization's Settings → Repository → General → Releases, choose All repositories. Only releases published afterwards are immutable, so publish a new one.

## Internet

### Internet: Attack surface

#### NSV-001: Database or cache open to the internet

**Severity:** High · **Attack path** · **Reads:** What Shodan has seen on the entity's addresses · [Internet docs](https://help.shodan.io/the-basics/what-is-shodan)

Shodan reached a database, cache or message broker on this address from the internet. Anyone can try passwords against it, use any vulnerability in it, or, for stores that need no password by default (Redis, MongoDB, Elasticsearch, Memcached, etcd, CouchDB), read and change the data directly.

**How to fix**

1. Close the port to the internet: in AWS, remove the security group rule that admits 0.0.0.0/0 or ::/0 on it; elsewhere, the host's firewall.
2. Reach the service from inside the network, or through a VPN, bastion or Cloudflare Tunnel.
3. Check the service's logs for connections you don't recognise.

#### NSV-002: Remote administration open to the internet

**Severity:** High · **Attack path** · **Reads:** What Shodan has seen on the entity's addresses · [Internet docs](https://help.shodan.io/the-basics/what-is-shodan)

Shodan reached a way to log in to or control this machine (SSH, Remote Desktop, VNC, SMB, a Docker or Kubernetes API) from the internet. These are tried with stolen and guessed passwords around the clock, and an unauthenticated Docker API or Kubelet is a way to run code at once.

**How to fix**

1. Close the port to the internet, or limit it to the addresses you work from.
2. Use AWS Systems Manager Session Manager, a VPN, a bastion or Cloudflare Access for remote access instead.
3. Never expose the Docker API without TLS.

#### NSV-003: Software with known vulnerabilities on an address the entity uses

**Severity:** Medium · **Reads:** What Shodan has seen on the entity's addresses · [Internet docs](https://help.shodan.io/the-basics/what-is-shodan)

Shodan matched the software it saw on this address to published vulnerabilities (CVEs). Shodan judges by the version the software announces, so a patched build can be listed by mistake, but attackers search Shodan the same way to find targets.

**How to fix**

1. Open the address on Shodan to see which service and version each vulnerability is for.
2. Update that software, or confirm the fix is backported and mark the finding a false positive.
3. If the service doesn't need to be on the internet, close it.

#### XP-012: Origin of a proxied hostname can be found on Shodan

**Severity:** Medium · **Attack path** · **Spans providers** · **Reads:** What Shodan has seen on the entity's addresses, Domains, DNS records and addresses of the entity's other accounts · [Cloudflare docs](https://developers.cloudflare.com/fundamentals/security/protect-your-origin-server/)

The hostname is proxied through Cloudflare to hide its origin, but Shodan lists the origin's address with the entity's hostnames, usually from the certificate the origin answers with. Anyone can search Shodan for the hostname, find the origin and send traffic straight to it, past the WAF, rate limits and Access.

**How to fix**

1. Let only Cloudflare reach the origin: in AWS or Alibaba Cloud, a security group that admits only Cloudflare's ranges (a prefix list keeps it current); elsewhere, the firewall.
2. Better, use a Cloudflare Tunnel so the origin has no open port.
3. Use Authenticated Origin Pulls, so the origin refuses connections without Cloudflare's client certificate.
4. Move the origin to a new address once it is locked, since the old one is known.

#### XP-013: Load balancer's target can be reached without the load balancer

**Severity:** High · **Attack path** · **Spans providers** · **Reads:** Load balancers, their rules and targets, and security groups in the entity's AWS accounts · [AWS docs](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/elasticloadbalancing/latest/application/load-balancer-update-security-groups.html)

The entity's hostname goes through a load balancer, but a target behind it has its own public address and security groups that let anyone reach the port it serves on. Anyone who finds that address (Shodan, certificate logs, an old DNS record) skips the load balancer and everything on it: the WAF, rate limits, TLS settings, and any sign-in the rule requires. Critical when the rule signs visitors in first: the application is reachable without signing in.

**How to fix**

1. Let only the load balancer reach its targets: in the target's security group, replace the rule that admits 0.0.0.0/0 or ::/0 on the target port with one that admits the load balancer's security group.
2. Move targets to private subnets without public addresses, so they can't be reached from the internet at all.
3. If the application checks who is signed in from the load balancer's headers, make it verify the header's signature, since a direct request can forge it.

#### XP-015: Load balancer still routes a hostname that DNS doesn't point at it

**Severity:** Low · **Spans providers** · **Reads:** Load balancers, their rules and targets, and security groups in the entity's AWS accounts, Domains, DNS records and addresses of the entity's other accounts · [AWS docs](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/elasticloadbalancing/latest/application/rule-condition-types.html#host-conditions)

An internet-facing load balancer has a rule for this hostname, but no DNS record sends it there any more. The application behind the rule is still reachable by anyone who sends that Host header to the load balancer, and old or staging applications left this way are rarely patched or watched.

**How to fix**

If the application is retired, delete the rule and its target group. If it is still needed, give it a DNS record and the same protection as the entity's other hostnames, or limit the rule to the addresses that use it (a source IP condition).

#### XP-025: Alibaba Cloud load balancer's backend server can be reached without the load balancer

**Severity:** High · **Attack path** · **Spans providers** · **Reads:** Load balancers, their rules and targets, and security groups in the entity's AWS accounts · [Alibaba Cloud docs](https://www.alibabacloud.com/help/en/slb/application-load-balancer/user-guide/add-an-alb-instance-to-a-security-group)

The entity's hostname goes through an Alibaba Cloud load balancer, but a backend server behind it has its own public address and security groups that let anyone reach the port it serves on. Anyone who finds that address (Shodan, certificate logs, an old DNS record) skips the load balancer and everything on it: WAF, access control lists and TLS settings.

**How to fix**

1. Let only the load balancer reach its backends: in the server's security group, replace the rule that admits 0.0.0.0/0 on the backend port with one that admits the load balancer's vSwitch range or security group.
2. Release the server's public address or EIP, so it can only be reached through the load balancer.

#### XP-027: Alibaba Cloud load balancer still routes a hostname that DNS doesn't point at it

**Severity:** Low · **Spans providers** · **Reads:** Load balancers, their rules and targets, and security groups in the entity's AWS accounts, Domains, DNS records and addresses of the entity's other accounts · [Alibaba Cloud docs](https://www.alibabacloud.com/help/en/slb/application-load-balancer/user-guide/manage-forwarding-rules-for-a-listener)

An internet-facing ALB has a forwarding rule for this hostname, but no DNS record sends it there any more. The application behind the rule is still reachable by anyone who sends that Host header to the load balancer, and old or staging applications left this way are rarely patched or watched.

**How to fix**

If the application is retired, delete the forwarding rule and its server group. If it is still needed, give it a DNS record and the same protection as the entity's other hostnames, or limit the rule to the addresses that use it (a source IP condition).

### Internet: TLS & HTTPS

#### NCT-001: Certificate issued by an authority the domain's CAA records don't allow

**Severity:** Medium · **Reads:** Certificate transparency logs (crt.sh), Public DNS lookups · [Cloudflare docs](https://developers.cloudflare.com/ssl/edge-certificates/caa-records/)

CAA records name the only certificate authorities that may issue for a domain. A recent certificate from another one means the records changed, an authority ignored them, or someone got a certificate for your name who shouldn't have, and could use it to impersonate the site.

**How to fix**

1. Open the certificate in the logs and find who requested it.
2. If it's yours, add its authority to the domain's CAA records.
3. If it isn't, ask the authority to revoke it and find how the name was validated (a dangling record, a compromised account, a hijacked email).

### Internet: DNS

#### NDS-001: Domain whose DNS isn't in any connected account

**Severity:** Low · **Reads:** Domains, DNS records and addresses of the entity's other accounts · [Cloudflare docs](https://developers.cloudflare.com/dns/zone-setups/full-setup/)

Keelson can only check the records of DNS it reads. Records on this domain that point at deleted servers, buckets or sites, or that publish an origin's address, go unnoticed, and the domain is often forgotten until someone takes over one of its names.

**How to fix**

1. Find where the domain's DNS is hosted from its nameservers.
2. If it is on a platform Keelson reads (Cloudflare or Route 53), add that account to this entity.
3. Otherwise consider moving its DNS to one, or remove the domain from the entity's domains if it isn't yours.

#### XP-014: Public hostname points at an internal load balancer

**Severity:** Low · **Spans providers** · **Reads:** Load balancers, their rules and targets, and security groups in the entity's AWS accounts · [AWS docs](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/elasticloadbalancing/latest/application/application-load-balancers.html#load-balancer-scheme)

The hostname is in public DNS but its load balancer is internal: it answers only inside its VPC, and its public name resolves to private addresses. Anyone can read the internal load balancer's name and the private addresses behind it, which maps the internal network, and the hostname doesn't work for anyone outside.

**How to fix**

Move the record to a private hosted zone (Route 53) that only the VPC resolves, or point it at an internet-facing load balancer if it is meant to be public. Delete it if nothing uses it.

#### XP-026: Public hostname points at an internal Alibaba Cloud load balancer

**Severity:** Low · **Spans providers** · **Reads:** Load balancers, their rules and targets, and security groups in the entity's AWS accounts · [Alibaba Cloud docs](https://www.alibabacloud.com/help/en/slb/application-load-balancer/user-guide/create-an-alb-instance)

The hostname is in public DNS but its load balancer is internal (intranet): it answers only inside its VPC. Anyone can read the internal load balancer's name and the private addresses behind it, which maps the internal network, and the hostname doesn't work for anyone outside.

**How to fix**

Move the record to Alibaba Cloud DNS PrivateZone, which only the VPC resolves, or point it at an internet-facing load balancer if it is meant to be public. Delete it if nothing uses it.
